name: physiologic changes in pregnancy overview
title: A finding in a pregnant patient: normal pregnancy or pathology? Seven columns (cardiac, respiratory and immune, renal, thyroid and sugar, gastrointestinal, anemia, low platelets), each giving what is normal with the number that marks its edge, what means pathology, and what to do

nodes.title: A finding in a pregnant patient: NORMAL pregnancy, or PATHOLOGY?
lines: progesterone relaxes smooth muscle + drives breathing · estrogen raises binding proteins · human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) peaks at 8–12 weeks

nodes.title: Vital signs + breathing
lines: symptoms do NOT separate normal from disease

nodes.title: Bloodwork + urine with a shifted normal
lines: a 'normal' lab value can be abnormal in pregnancy

nodes.title: Blood count: DILUTION + POOLING, or disease?
lines: anemia and low platelets are near universal

nodes.title: Cardiac
lines: vascular resistance ↓ · cardiac output ↑ 40%

nodes.title: Respiratory + immune
lines: progesterone ↑ ventilation · cell-mediated immunity ↓

nodes.title: Renal
lines: renal blood flow ↑ 60–80% → filtration ↑

nodes.title: Thyroid + sugar
lines: hCG acts like thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH)

nodes.title: Gastrointestinal
lines: progesterone slows the whole gut

nodes.title: Anemia
lines: plasma ↑ 30–50% > red cells ↑ 20–30%

nodes.title: Low platelets
lines: fall in EVERY pregnancy: spleen + placenta pooling, dilution

nodes.title: Blood pressure ↓
lines: lowest at 22–24 weeks

nodes.title: Heart rate ↑ ~10
lines: median 82 at 12 weeks → 91 at 34 weeks

nodes.title: Palpitations common
lines: more aware of a bigger plasma volume

nodes.title: Dyspnea in 60–75%
lines: from the 1st trimester, levels off in the 3rd

nodes.title: Rate UNCHANGED, tidal volume ↑
lines: compensated respiratory alkalosis: pH normal, bicarbonate slightly ↓

nodes.title: Proteinuria up to 30 mg/mmol
lines: urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (uPCR), or 300 mg/day on a 24-hour urine

nodes.title: Right > left hydronephrosis · glucosuria
lines: frequency + nocturia

nodes.title: TOTAL T4 ↑, FREE T4 steady
lines: estrogen ↑ thyroid binding globulin

nodes.title: 1st trimester: TSH slightly ↓
lines: the hCG peak acts on the TSH receptor

nodes.title: Very high hCG (hyperemesis): TSH quite ↓
lines: transient → OBSERVE, don't treat

nodes.title: Constipation · bloating
lines: reflux in over half · nausea + vomiting in most

nodes.title: Alkaline phosphatase ↑
lines: made by the placenta, not the liver

nodes.title: Lipids ↑
lines: triglycerides + LDL

nodes.title: DILUTION: the commonest cause
lines: anemia = hemoglobin < 110 (1st trimester), < 105 (2nd + 3rd)

nodes.title: Screen: 1st trimester + 24–28 weeks
lines: symptoms are common in pregnancy anyway

nodes.title: Gestational thrombocytopenia
lines: starts mid-to-late 2nd trimester
rarely < 100,000 · baby unaffected

nodes.title: No test proves it
lines: a diagnosis of EXCLUSION

nodes.title: Resting heart rate > 110
lines: the upper limit is still ~110: don't write tachycardia off

nodes.title: Palpitations: supraventricular tachycardia
lines: pregnancy can bring its first presentation

nodes.title: Dyspnea from a pulmonary embolism (PE) or pneumonia
lines: hard to tell from dyspnea of pregnancy

nodes.title: Influenza is MORE severe
lines: preterm delivery, pneumonia, intensive care, death

nodes.title: Creatinine in the 80s or above
lines: the lab may still call it 'normal'

nodes.title: uPCR > 30
lines: a clue to preeclampsia: see the HYPERTENSION IN PREGNANCY chart

nodes.title: Graves disease
lines: vs gestational transient thyrotoxicosis

nodes.title: Gestational diabetes
lines: insulin resistance tips her over

nodes.title: Gallstones
lines: more common in pregnancy

nodes.title: 1 · Ferritin < 30 → IRON deficiency
lines: or transferrin saturation < 20% if inflamed
the commonest disease · pica, restless legs

nodes.title: 2 · VERY low mean cell volume
lines: → hemoglobinopathy screen (thalassemia)
→ hematology + test the PARTNER

nodes.title: 3 · Macrocytic → B12 level
lines: → B12 1000–2000 mcg by mouth daily

nodes.title: < 100,000 or EARLY onset → immune thrombocytopenia (ITP)
lines: bleeding with past procedures · not normal post partum

nodes.title: + hypertension → preeclampsia or HELLP
lines: hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, low platelets
normotensive in 15%: check EVERYONE

nodes.title: + anemia + renal impairment: CAN'T MISS
lines: disseminated intravascular coagulation · thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura

nodes.title: IV fluid: judicious + monitored
lines: oncotic pressure ↓ → pulmonary edema risk ↑

nodes.title: LOWER threshold to look for PE or deep vein thrombosis
lines: pregnancy is PRO-THROMBOTIC
D-dimer ↑ in every pregnancy: alone it proves nothing

nodes.title: Flu shot + oseltamivir: SAFE
lines: vaccines in pregnancy: ANTENATAL CARE chart

nodes.title: Glucosuria is NOT a diabetes screen
Already hypothyroid → DOUBLE levothyroxine Saturday + Sunday
TIGHTER sugar targets than usual
lines: hyperglycemia is a teratogen

nodes.title: Don't measure lipids
lines: an isolated rise needs no treatment

nodes.title: 1 · Oral iron, daily or every other day
lines: with vitamin C, away from calcium, dairy, coffee, tea
2 weeks: hemoglobin ↑ ≥ 1 g/dL → continue

nodes.title: 2 · IV iron sucrose (NOT 1st trimester)
lines: oral fails or not tolerated · hemoglobin < 100
3rd trimester or delivery close

nodes.title: ITP: prednisone (NOT dexamethasone) · IV immunoglobulin if late 3rd trimester
lines: baby: platelets at birth, no difficult instrumental delivery

panels.title: Platelets needed for delivery
items: vaginal delivery 30,000 (some aim for 50,000) · cesarean section 50,000 · spinal or epidural 70,000–80,000
